charts.title: Revenue by Segment
charts.annotation: Nine discloses the segment split only in half-year results, so points are sparse (H1 FY2024-FY2026). Publishing and Digital Publishing are near-identical values across filings and likely the same segment under two labels; Domain ends after the Domain Group sale completed in FY2026.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Nine Entertainment Co. Holdings Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Nine Entertainment Co. Holdings Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Nine Entertainment Co. Holdings Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Nine Entertainment Co. Holdings Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Nine Entertainment Co. Holdings Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Nine Entertainment Co. Holdings Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Nine Entertainment Co. Holdings Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

capexMix.title: CapEx composition
capexMix.content:
Total CapEx split between property, plant & equipment (studios, broadcast towers, transmission gear, offices) and capitalised intangibles (software, mainly Stan's streaming platform and digital publishing systems).

For Nine Entertainment Co. Holdings Limited: the mix has shifted toward intangibles as Stan has scaled, from roughly a fifth of CapEx a decade ago to often exceeding the PP&E line -- a tell for how much of the group's reinvestment is now software/content-platform spend rather than physical broadcast infrastructure.

What to watch:

  • Intangible CapEx growing faster than Streaming segment revenue (platform spend outrunning payback)
  • PP&E CapEx spikes around studio or transmission upgrades

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue mix
segmentRevenue.content:
Nine reports four (historically five, including Domain) reporting segments: Broadcasting (Total TV, free-to-air), Stan/Streaming (subscription video), Publishing (The Age, SMH, digital subscriptions and classifieds) and, until its FY2026 divestiture, Domain (property classifieds).

For Nine Entertainment Co. Holdings Limited: the thesis is the mix shift away from linear TV advertising (cyclical, ad-market exposed) toward Stan subscriptions and Publishing digital subscriptions (more recurring); the Domain sale removed a high-growth, high-multiple segment and concentrated the group back on media. Segment detail is only disclosed at half-year, so the chart has few points.

What to watch:

  • Broadcasting share of total revenue shrinking over time
  • Stan/Streaming growth rate versus subscriber and ARPU trends elsewhere in this dashboard
  • Whether Publishing and Digital Publishing are reported as one segment or two in a given period -- the two series often carry near-identical values

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Nine Entertainment Co. Holdings Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Nine Entertainment Co. Holdings Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
